headline_marked: [[Durga Puja]] festivities begin with Mahalaya observance across Bangladesh
headline: Durga Puja festivities begin with Mahalaya observance across Bangladesh
summary: Hindu devotees welcomed the Goddess Durga with Chandi recitation and prayers, marking the start of the festive season and the countdown to the main Puja.
details: The auspicious occasion of Mahalaya today marks the beginning of the main Durga Puja festivities for the Hindu community. Devotees across Bangladesh are welcoming the Goddess Durga by reciting Chandi texts and singing 'Agamani' songs, signifying the start of 'Debipaksha' and the final countdown to the Puja.

In Dhaka, special rituals including Chandi recitation and 'Pitri Tarpan' (offering to ancestors) began at the Dhakeshwari National Temple from Saturday morning. Thousands of devotees gathered, praying for the destruction of evil forces and the well-being of humanity.
The Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Chandra, attended the event at the Dhakeshwari National Temple. He extended his greetings and wished for lasting peace and welfare for all.
Meanwhile, at the Banani ground in Dhaka, the Gulshan-Banani Puja Foundation organized a colorful Mahalaya event. The Prime Minister's Advisor on Education, Mahdee Amin, was the chief guest.

Addressing the gathering, Mahdee Amin emphasized unity, stating that all citizens of the country should identify themselves solely as 'Bangladeshi', transcending religious and ethnic differences. He highlighted the government's commitment to fostering an environment of mutual harmony and solidarity.

Amin also mentioned that the government has increased financial grants and allocations for Puja mandaps to ensure the Durga Puja is celebrated smoothly and joyfully. The event was also attended by the Deputy High Commissioner of India in Dhaka, Pawan Kumar Banej, and leaders of the Puja Celebration Committee.
caption:

The Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Chandra, attended the event at the Dhakeshwari National Temple. He extended his greetings and wished for lasting peace and welfare for all.

headline_marked: CNG driver [[raped and killed 15-year-old student]] in Comilla
headline: CNG driver raped and killed 15-year-old student in Comilla
summary: The victim, Jannatul Tazmin, was lured away from her destination by the driver; police have arrested the suspect in Chittagong.
details: A 15-year-old schoolgirl, Jannatul Tazmin, was raped and murdered by an auto-rickshaw driver named Suman Mia (35), police reported during a press conference on Saturday.
On October 8, the victim's body was found in a paddy field in Bhoraljagpur village of Lalmai Upazila, Comilla, following a call to the National Emergency Service (999).
Tazmin, a 7th-grade student at Farida Bidyatan in Comilla city, was originally from Jessore but lived in the Rescourse area of Comilla due to her father's job.
The suspect, Suman Mia, was hired by the victim on October 8 at the Tisha Bus Counter on the World Road of Padua Bazar to take her home to Rescourse for 300 BDT.
Instead of taking the shortcut he promised, the driver diverted the route toward the crime scene in a secluded, dark area. When the victim tried to escape, the suspect strangled her with a towel.
During interrogation, Suman Mia confessed to raping the victim before killing her by pressing her head into the ground with his foot to ensure her death.
The suspect then stole the victim's iPhone and hid it in a jungle near a pond in the Jhalmuri Bazar area before fleeing to Chittagong.
Police arrested Suman Mia in Chittagong on October 9 and recovered the stolen iPhone based on his confession and guidance.
caption:
A 15-year-old student was lured away by her CNG driver, raped, and killed in Comilla. The suspect has been arrested.

A 15-year-old schoolgirl, Jannatul Tazmin, was raped and murdered by an auto-rickshaw driver named Suman Mia (35), police reported during a press conference on Saturday.

On October 8, the victim's body was found in a paddy field in Bhoraljagpur village of Lalmai Upazila, Comilla, following a call to the National Emergency Service (999).

Tazmin, a 7th-grade student at Farida Bidyatan in Comilla city, was originally from Jessore but lived in the Rescourse area of Comilla due to her father's job.

The suspect, Suman Mia, was hired by the victim on October 8 at the Tisha Bus Counter on the World Road of Padua Bazar to take her home to Rescourse for 300 BDT.

Instead of taking the shortcut he promised, the driver diverted the route toward the crime scene in a secluded, dark area. When the victim tried to escape, the suspect strangled her with a towel.

During interrogation, Suman Mia confessed to raping the victim before killing her by pressing her head into the ground with his foot to ensure her death.

The suspect then stole the victim's iPhone and hid it in a jungle near a pond in the Jhalmuri Bazar area before fleeing to Chittagong.

Police arrested Suman Mia in Chittagong on October 9 and recovered the stolen iPhone based on his confession and guidance.
